summary: Blackwell Tonkawa Municipal Airport (BWL/KBKN) is a small general aviation facility located in Kay County, northern Oklahoma, serving the cities of Blackwell and nearby Tonkawa. The airport features a single asphalt runway and primarily supports private aircraft, flight training, and local aviation activity. It provides convenient air access to the north-central Oklahoma region, situated roughly midway between Oklahoma City and Wichita, Kansas.
faqs:
Q: What type of airport is Blackwell Tonkawa Municipal Airport?
A: It is a small general aviation airport primarily serving private and recreational pilots, with no scheduled commercial airline service.

Q: Where is the airport located in relation to nearby cities?
A: The airport is on the eastern side of Blackwell, Oklahoma, about 5 miles from Tonkawa, and roughly 100 miles south of Wichita, Kansas.

Q: How many runways does the airport have?
A: The airport has a single asphalt runway, designated 17/35, suitable for small to medium general aviation aircraft.

Q: Are there fuel services available at the airport?
A: Self-service fuel is typically available for general aviation pilots, though hours may vary; pilots should check current NOTAMs before arrival.
transport_tips: Reaching the airport requires a personal vehicle, as there is no public transit service to the facility. Blackwell is accessible via US Highway 177 and State Highway 11, with the airport located just minutes from downtown. Rental cars are not available on-site, so arranging ground transportation in advance is recommended for visitors.
local_tip: If you're visiting during warmer months, consider taking a short drive to nearby Tonkawa to visit the Tonkawa Tribal Museum or enjoy a meal at one of the local diners—it's a genuine slice of small-town Oklahoma hospitality.
